findings.headline: 99215 on 31.7% of claims vs 5.9% expected; 10 of 14 sampled 99215 charts documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: The 99215 share is high at every complexity level, including 18% on patients with no chronic conditions. A complete random sample of 30 charts had 14 below the billed level, and 10 of the 14 documented 99215s were below it (peer rule baseline 15%, raw comparison 42%). Note checks are near baseline and no audit trail was requested. The random-sample overpayment draft is about $3,708 (CI $2,595 to $4,821) and is reliable. No data-quality flags. A coder needs to confirm.

findings.headline: 99215 on 19.4% vs 4.4% expected; 9 of 21 sampled 99214/99215 charts documented below the billed level
findings.interpretation: The panel is low-acuity (no patients with 4 or more conditions), and 64% of its 99215s are on patients with 0 or 1 conditions. A complete random sample of 30 had 10 below the billed level, and 9 of the 21 documented 99214/99215s were below it (43% vs a 9% peer rate). 3 of 14 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review had no test line on the claim. The overpayment draft is about $2,922 (CI $1,709 to $4,136) and is reliable. No data-quality flags.

findings.headline: 99215 on 22.8% vs 6.3% expected; 6 of 7 sampled 99215 charts documented at moderate MDM
findings.interpretation: A complete random sample of 30 had 11 below the billed level. Only 7 of the sampled charts were 99215s, so the overpayment estimate is not reliable and is not quoted. 30% of notes were flagged as duplicates, which suggests copy-forward. Rates are not proof. A targeted 99215 follow-up (which would not support extrapolation) could firm this up. No data-quality flags.

findings.headline: Most extreme claims outlier (99215 on 50.4% vs 8.1% expected), but charts and audit trail support the billed levels
findings.interpretation: 99215 is billed far above peers at every complexity level, including 26% on patients with no chronic conditions, so panel acuity alone does not explain it. But 0 of 30 random charts were below the billed level. The EHR audit trail showed no bulk-created or paste-heavy notes, and the problems-addressed rate (23%) is in line with other providers. Charts do not support an upcoding lean. Recommend a human coder review of the 99215s on low-complexity patients.

findings.headline: 99215 on 20.1% vs 4.8% expected; only 12 of 30 random charts returned, 3 below the billed level
findings.interpretation: The claims pattern is elevated even on patients with no chronic conditions (14.6%). The office returned 12 of 30 charts and did not answer the follow-up for the missing visits. A partial return can be biased in either direction, and 3 of 12 below the billed level is not decisive. Only 2 of the returned charts were 99215s, so the overpayment estimate is not reliable. A complete sample is needed to judge.

findings.headline: 99215 on 26.8% vs 6.1% expected; 1 of 29 random charts below the billed level
findings.interpretation: Charts largely support the billing and note checks are near baseline. 99215 shares rise steeply with complexity (75% on patients with 5 or more conditions), which partly fits a sicker panel. But low-complexity 99215 shares are still about 3 times peers, so this is not a clean high-acuity pattern either.

findings.headline: 99215 on 19.0% vs 5.2% expected; 0 of 29 random charts below the billed level
findings.interpretation: Documentation supports the billed levels. The excess is concentrated in patients with 4 or more conditions, which is more consistent with a high-acuity panel, but low-complexity shares are also about 2 to 3 times peers. No upcoding lean.

findings.headline: 99215 on 14.5% vs 4.8% expected; 0 of 28 random charts below the billed level
